headline: High-risk shared-project writes and unverified output chaining make gpt-engineer → Superset pair unsafe by default for code and data workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-engineer writes files in a shared project directory and has no self-isolation by default; Superset exposes an API and can consume project artifacts or copied outputs. That creates a plausible instruction-hijack path through shared files, though no direct automatic channel is documented, so I rate it medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same project directory without provenance tagging, prompt-like content can be interpreted as instructions.
IF Superset ingests files or text produced by gpt-engineer, attacker-controlled content can steer downstream behavior.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories.
Add a manual review step before Superset consumes any gpt-engineer output.
Prefix generated artifacts with machine-readable provenance headers.
Disable any automatic file-to-instruction parsing in the workflow.
requires-engineering: add content provenance and sanitization gates.

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-engineer reads and writes the user project directory and can send prompts to configured model APIs; Superset has API access and allowlisted egress. If sensitive files live in the shared workspace, both agents can expose them through their respective outbound paths, so the leakage risk is medium.
conditions: IF the shared project directory contains secrets or regulated data, gpt-engineer can read them.
IF Superset is configured to query external services or APIs with workspace-derived content, that content can leave the environment.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared project directory.
Use separate service accounts and API keys for each agent.
Restrict Superset to non-sensitive datasets only.
Review outbound requests from both agents before enabling them.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data classification filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: gpt-engineer has filesystem write access and per-project shared state across instances; Superset can call APIs and has allowlisted egress. In a shared workspace, concurrent writes and API-driven updates can collide without locking, and the profiles do not show coordination primitives, so the conflict is high.
conditions: IF both agents modify the same project directory concurrently, file races can corrupt outputs.
IF Superset writes back derived artifacts while gpt-engineer is regenerating files, state divergence can occur.
mitigations: Run only one writer at a time.
Assign disjoint directories to each agent.
Take a manual snapshot before each run.
Disable any automated write-back from Superset.
requires-engineering: add file locking or transactional workspace coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-engineer produces generated code that Superset may treat as authoritative input for analytics or downstream actions. Because the profiles do not document a verification boundary, the pair can propagate mistakes from code generation into later decisions, but the blast radius is not clearly irreversible by default.
conditions: IF Superset consumes gpt-engineer output without human verification, incorrect code or metadata can cascade into later actions.
IF generated artifacts are used as source-of-truth for dashboards or automation, errors can be amplified.
mitigations: Require human review of generated artifacts.
Compare outputs against a known-good baseline.
Mark gpt-engineer output as untrusted until validated.
Limit Superset to read-only analysis of reviewed artifacts.
requires-engineering: add automated validation between generation and consumption.

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and the profiles do not show a residency, certification, or retention mismatch. The only concrete compliance concern is that gpt-engineer handles an OpenAI API key while Superset has no stated sensitive-data handling, so no pair-specific breach is evident from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the shared project directory, compliance obligations may arise outside the documented profiles.
IF either deployment adds a non-local retention policy, the pair may need additional controls.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace.
Document retention and deletion rules for both tools.
Review API-key handling for gpt-engineer.
Confirm Superset deployment policies before use.
requires-engineering: add formal residency and retention controls.
